F1 Drivers Criticize New Madrid Track for Safety and Racing Concerns

Formula 1 drivers have expressed significant dissatisfaction with the new Madrid Grand Prix track, citing concerns about safety and the quality of racing. Several drivers described the circuit as "not good for racing" and one outlet referred to it as a "car killer." The primary issues raised by drivers include the track's design, which they believe poses a danger and hinders competitive racing. These criticisms suggest a potential need for redesigns to improve the circuit's suitability for the sport.
